solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clear run into bay

indicators.note: run is put into bay, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for a bay

parts.note: a bight is a bay or curve in a coastline
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A clear run straight into a bay, as for a sailor or a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and bright are synonyms for weather or a sky that is cloudless and sunny.

clue.text: The most built-up BBC party repeatedly curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the BBC nickname loses its final letter

parts.note: the Beeb is the nickname of the British Broadcasting Corporation

indicators.note: repeatedly says the curtailing happens again, so the party word also loses its last letter

parts.note: a fiesta is a festive party

explanation.surface: The most developed area hosts a BBC party that keeps being cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built-up' suggests a developed urban area, but here it means muscular.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy describes a burly muscular build, so the beefiest person is the most powerfully built.

clue.text: Mostly charge language group

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the charge word is kept

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime

explanation.surface: A tour company mostly charges a group by its language.
explanation.definitionFit: Indic is the branch of Indo-European languages spoken across northern India, Hindi and Bengali among them.

clue.text: Call The Oval every so often

indicators.note: only some letters of the words, at regular gaps, are taken

explanation.surface: Phoning the Oval cricket ground now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground. Taking every second letter gives a rare call meaning stop, found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoa is an old cry used to attract attention or to call a halt, a variant of ho.

clue.text: Supply yard shut for 24 hours

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, meaning in a flexible way, so the letters that follow are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to deliveries: the supply yard is closed for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun qualifying 'yard', but it is the adverb from supple, the anagram signal. The whole puzzle salutes Inspector Morse: Thursday, Strange, Bright, Endeavour and Morse are all names from the series.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday is one particular day of the week, a stretch lasting a full day and night.

clue.text: Tough Henry going over freezing plain

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: in a down clue, the plain word turns over, reading upward

parts.note: a tundra is a vast treeless frozen Arctic plain

explanation.surface: A hardy explorer called Henry crosses a frozen plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough as a noun means a rough, aggressive man, as does a hard nut.

clue.text: Me ram's horny, moving around sheep

indicators.note: the letters are moved about to make a new order

explanation.surface: A ram declares his lust as he circles the ewes.
explanation.walkthrough: Romney Marsh is a stretch of Kent and also a breed of sheep from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romney Marsh is a hardy long-wool breed of sheep named after the Kent marshland.

clue.text: European town takes little time to track 500 weapons

indicators.note: to track is to follow, so the little time pieces follow the earlier ones

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
arms are weapons
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A town that gives a short time to tracking a shipment of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Darmstadt in Germany gave its name to darmstadtium, element 110.
explanation.definitionFit: Darmstadt is a city in Hesse, Germany, home to a heavy-ion research centre.

clue.text: Delivers products

definitions.meaning: the outputs or returns from a crop or investment

explanation.surface: A factory delivers its products.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields can be a verb for giving up or producing, and a plural noun for amounts produced.

clue.text: Uniform has got carried outside boundary

indicators.note: carried goes outside the uniform letter, enclosing it

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A soldier in uniform carried across the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourne is an archaic word for a limit or boundary, as in Hamlet's undiscovered country.

clue.text: Try an overdue alternative

indicators.note: an alternative form of the words an overdue, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to try a different option for something long overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to attempt or make an effort, a formal synonym of try.

clue.text: Telegraph characters sent over in Times Roman

indicators.note: sent over says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the printed words Times Roman

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Newspaper type: the Telegraph's letters dispatched in the Times's typeface, Times Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden step: 'in' is it. 'Telegraph' looks like the rival newspaper, but here it is the telegraph machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code is the set of dots and dashes used to send each letter over a telegraph line.

clue.text: Lack of clarity in firm about cuts therefore

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: about cuts therefore says the word for about is cut into the word for therefore

parts.note: hence means therefore, for that reason
re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A complaint that a company memo about job cuts is muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherence is speech or thought that does not hang together, so it lacks clarity.

clue.text: Second- or higher-level gear?

parts.note: second-hand clothes passed on from an older sibling, one level higher in the family, read as if gearbox settings

explanation.surface: A question about choosing second gear or higher in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' points to a gearbox, but means clothes: second-hand ones handed down from higher up the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes handed on from an older sibling are second-hand garments passed down from someone senior.

clue.text: Polish knight has gone blue

indicators.note: the knight has gone, so its letter is removed from the word for polish

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth or polish it
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A Polish knight's armour has turned blue, or he has grown gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like the nationality; it is the verb to polish. The knight is N, as in chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is an idiom for feeling low or unhappy.

clue.text: Brief way to classify rum

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a way
to range things is to arrange or class them in order

explanation.surface: A short guide to grading rums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is dated British slang for odd or peculiar, just as strange is.

clue.text: Strengthen means of controlling stallion?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the pull of the reins that a rider uses to control a horse

explanation.surface: A query about ways of strengthening control over a stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, the force applied through a rein.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcing a wall or an argument means adding support to make it stronger.

clue.text: Queen's consort needing diplomacy from east to keep order

indicators.note: the diplomacy word is made to keep the order, holding it inside
read from the east, that is right to left in an across clue, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: tact is delicacy and diplomacy in dealing with people
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Prince Philip as the Queen's consort, needing tact and keeping order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen suggests royalty, but a queen is a female cat and her mate is a tom. The OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour in the gift of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a breeding female cat, so her male partner is a tom.

clue.text: Hibernian second team showing guts, finding area for crossing?

parts.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so Hibernian means Irish

indicators.note: the guts are the inner letters, so the middle of team is shown

explanation.surface: Hibernian, the Edinburgh football club, fields a gutsy reserve side and finds space for crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian looks like the Scottish football club; here it means Irish. 'crossing' means a sea passage, not a football cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea lies between Britain and Ireland and is crossed by ferry routes.

clue.text: Thingumajigs go amiss when article drops off

indicators.note: the article drops off, so its letter leaves the pool of go amiss, and what is left goes wrong, into a new order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Gadgets go wrong when a part falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amiss' works twice: it is part of the letters, and 'go amiss' (go wrong) also says to rearrange GO MISS, what is left once 'drops off' removes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Gismos and thingumajigs are both informal words for gadgets whose names escape you.

clue.text: Pan placed to hold ice

indicators.note: the placed word holds the ice word inside it

parts.note: set means put or placed
to ice someone is gangster slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A pan set down to hold ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' looks like frozen water but is slang for murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan, especially a heavy cast-iron one.

clue.text: One in charge having dog roll over

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: rolled over means turned around, so the word for roll is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roll or list of duties

explanation.surface: A keeper whose dog rolls over on command.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the person responsible for a museum collection or exhibition.

clue.text: About to drop stick

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to leave someone somewhere is to drop them off

explanation.surface: Someone about to let go of a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleave means both split and its opposite, cling; here it is cling.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave to something is to cling or adhere to it, as stick does.

clue.text: After pub fire, finish off wine

indicators.note: the fire word comes after the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the fire word has its finish, its final letter, taken off

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: After a fire at the pub, someone drinks up the last of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux wine from the commune of that name in Sauternes.

clue.text: Chap in East London semi

indicators.note: Cockney speech of East London drops the initial aitch, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: semi means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: A man living in a semi-detached house in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' looks like a British semi-detached house, but here it is the prefix meaning half. Cockneys drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Alf is a man's name, and crosswords use any common name to stand for a chap.

clue.text: Dodgy adverts fish for items in transmission

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fishy adverts for car parts that might not be what they claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmission' looks like broadcasting, which fits adverts, but it is the drive mechanism of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive shafts are the rotating rods that carry power from gearbox to wheels, parts of a vehicle's drivetrain.

clue.text: Imagine two girls getting mixed up?

indicators.note: the two names are muddled together, each swapping its second half with the other

parts.note: Fanny and Nancy are girls' names

explanation.surface: Picture a pair of girls being confused for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: FANNY and NANCY swap halves to make FAN+CY and NAN+NY; keep the first. The blogger was unsure too, calling it a hybrid of the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine or suppose it, as in fancy that.

clue.text: Spread last bit of sour pickle around

indicators.note: the pickle word goes around the letter taken from sour

parts.note: to be in a stew or a pickle is to be in a mess

indicators.note: the final letter of the word sour is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for spreading a sour pickle around a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' suggests a relish, but here it means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to scatter things loosely over a surface, a sense of spread.

clue.text: Famous victory boy breaking records noted expressions of admiration

indicators.note: the victory and boy words break into the records word, splitting it apart

parts.note: logs are written records, as in a ship's log
VE Day marked victory in Europe in 1945
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A sports star, famous after a victory, breaks records and is admired.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day (8 May 1945) celebrated Allied victory in Europe. 'noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Love songs are pieces of music expressing devotion, admiration put to notes.

clue.text: Dance music recalled in haikus, oddly

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in reverse
taking letters irregularly, every other one of the word

explanation.surface: Dance music remembered in a set of strange haikus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican music style with offbeat rhythms, a forerunner of reggae, made for dancing.

clue.text: In endless crawl, old wino consumed oily liquid

indicators.note: the old wino pieces sit in the shortened crawl word
the shortened crawl word consumes, or takes in, the wino letters
endless means the crawl word loses its final letter

parts.note: to creep is to crawl slowly
a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: An old drunk crawls along, having swallowed something oily.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a dark oily distillate of tar painted on fences as a wood preservative.

clue.text: Lecherous female took chair by unknown artist

parts.note: to sit is to take a chair, and sat is its past tense
y is one of the algebraic letters for an unknown quantity
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A woman sat for a portrait by an anonymous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyra is a female satyr, and satyrs are mythical figures of unbridled lust.
